scientific_question: In an independent repeated-batch food-waste digestion study, do bottles run under a biochar regime produce a different early cumulative methane yield than same-laboratory unamended bottles, and is the direction the same in both laboratories?

prediction_target.quantity: cumulative methane yield at a fixed within-batch horizon
prediction_target.unit_requirement: Only within-laboratory ratios are computed. The source unit is unverified, and a log response ratio is invariant to a shared multiplicative unit, so no unit conversion is performed or needed.
prediction_target.effect_scale: log response ratio of bottle-level geometric mean yields

reasons: No model or effect estimate in the repository is commensurate with this target: Kozlowski 2025 reports fitted asymptotic potential and maximum rate from single fresh-inoculum BMP runs, not fixed-horizon yield in acclimated repeated batches.
Development doses are g/L; Sanglier doses are labels 1/2 whose gram basis differs between laboratories and whose BRL w:w basis cannot be verified.
No biochar material descriptors for Sanglier are committed, so no descriptor-conditioned model can be evaluated without refitting.
Development evidence gives no sign-unambiguous prediction for early yield: Kozlowski pyrolysis biochar shows +4.5% potential but -7.4% maximum rate.

exploratory.note: The two laboratories share one study, protocol family and author team. Agreement between them is cross-laboratory reproducibility inside one study, not cross-study generalization (question B).

independence_rule: Bottles are the independent experimental units. Repeated batches of one bottle share recirculated digestate and are repeated measures, never independent replicates. AMPTShort rows are a 12-hour derivative of one continuous record and are never counted as observations for inference.
inclusion_criteria: Cycle adjudication class is source_consistent or resolvable_from_source.
Cycle lies inside its laboratory's clean batch window (see temporal_definition).
Bottle has an admissible cycle for every batch of its laboratory window.
Arm is one of the allowable treatments for that laboratory.
exclusion_criteria: Any cycle classed conflicting, ambiguous or excluded.
Any cycle with a recorded co-intervention rule: R3, R4, R5, R9 or R10.
A whole bottle when any cycle inside its laboratory window fails admission, because digestate carry-over propagates exposure and faults to later cycles.
A cycle without a methane yield observation exactly at the horizon (no interpolation).
Poor or failed methane production is never an exclusion criterion; outcome events (Events!6, Events!7) remain in the data.

excluded_arms_primary.LBE [1]+: Meaning of '+' before batch 11 is undocumented (rule R6, ambiguous).
excluded_arms_primary.LBE [2]+: Meaning of '+' before batch 11 is undocumented (rule R6, ambiguous).

treatment_reconstruction_rules.regime_assignment: Bottle-level regime from the Inoculation condition label, the AMPTShort Biochar label and the recorded biochar grams, which must agree in every cycle used.
treatment_reconstruction_rules.event_scope: A laboratory event changes a bottle's exposure only when its text names that bottle or its condition (results/validation/sanglier_2022_event_scope.csv). An unspecified-subset event makes every overlapping cycle in that laboratory ambiguous.
treatment_reconstruction_rules.source_values: Original labels, grams and volumes are retained; adjudication adds classes and evidence but never overwrites a source value.

temporal_definition.time_origin: First observed time of each laboratory/batch (within_batch_days).
temporal_definition.clean_window_rule: For each laboratory, consecutive batches from batch 1 up to, but excluding, the first batch in which any cycle triggers a laboratory-scope co-intervention or unspecified-subset rule (R4 without a named condition, R8, R9).
temporal_definition.horizon_rule: Largest multiple of 0.5 day not exceeding the shortest last-observed within-batch time among admitted cycles.

repeated_batch_handling: Each bottle is summarised by the mean of ln(yield at horizon) over its window batches. Every admitted bottle contributes the same batches, so shared substrate-lot effects cancel between arms.
carryover_handling: A conflicting or excluded cycle removes the whole bottle from the primary analysis (rules R1, R2, R7). Residual-ammonia carry-over (R10) is ambiguous and excluded.
co_intervention_handling: Ammonium bicarbonate, trace-element regime changes and undocumented '+' labels are never attributed to biochar. Windows end before they begin.
normalization: None beyond the source's own per-substrate-VS yield. No blank subtraction (the design has no inoculum-only blanks). No cross-laboratory normalization.

leakage_prevention.admission_outcome_blindness: The admission step receives no methane volume, flow or yield column; it fails if one is present.

transfer_rules.role_rule: No refit: locked_external_validation. Only calibration parameters refit: calibration_transfer. Any structural or effect parameter refit: model_updating. Hypothesis or model chosen after viewing this data: exploratory.

development_comparator.use: Interval overlap is reported for context and is never scored as validation.

metrics.primary: Per laboratory and arm: log response ratio versus the same-laboratory control with a Welch 95% t interval over bottle summaries, plus an exact two-sided permutation p-value over bottle labels and its minimum attainable value.
secondary: S1 variance decomposition of ln(yield at horizon) into batch, arm and bottle-within-arm components per laboratory.
S2 cycle plateau audit: share of admitted cycles whose final 24 h increment is below 1% of cumulative yield.
S3 exploratory per-cycle modified Gompertz fits: relative standard error of potential and potential-rate correlation.
S4 count of independent experimental units available for any machine-learning model.
sensitivity: SA1 include LBE [1]+ and [2]+ as separate arms.
SA2 exclude control bottle IV.3 (reported failure) to show its influence; the primary analysis keeps it.
SA3 exclude IV.5 and IV.8 only in batch 1 by using LBE batches 2-8.

uncertainty_reporting: Report n bottles per arm, Welch degrees of freedom, interval, permutation p and its floor. Arms with fewer than three bottles carry low_replication=true. No z-intervals as primary for n below 30.

decision_rule.not_evaluable: Fewer than two bottles in either arm.
decision_rule.cross_laboratory_agreement: Labels 1 and 2 agree only if both laboratories give the same non-inconclusive verdict.

failure_criteria: Spec hash differs from the hash recorded at admission: stop.
Observed clean windows or horizon differ from expected values: stop and re-register.
Leakage audit finds a Sanglier identifier in a development path: stop.
Any admitted cycle lacks a yield exactly at the horizon: report the cycle as not evaluable; if a bottle loses a window batch, drop the bottle and report it.
Directional verdicts disagree between laboratories: report as failure of cross-laboratory reproducibility, not as noise to average away.
No arm reaches a non-inconclusive verdict: report the dataset as insufficient to resolve the effect at this replication.
outcome_exposure_disclosure: Before freezing, the analyst viewed final per-cycle yields of LBE bottles IV.1, IV.2, IV.3, IV.5 and IV.8 to check event statements, and the yield = volume / substrate VS identity. No arm-level summary or contrast was computed. Treatment of IV.3 follows the pre-existing repository rule that poor outcomes are not exclusions (docs/SANGLIER_2022_CONTEXT_AUDIT.md). The source deposit also states that biochar improved methane yield, so a directional agreement is not a blind test.
claims_prohibited_regardless_of_result: external validation of any kinetic, dose-response or global model
